summary: When a hero with no gloves wields a cockatrice corpse, the C path reports “You wield the cockatrice corpse in your bare hands.” and calls instapetrify(); the JavaScript helper reports the wield message but records note_unported instead of calling the existing instapetrify implementation. This is the first mismatch at step 48. The actionable source owner is wield.c:cant_wield_corpse().

source.branch: If the hero lacks gloves, the object is a corpse, its species touch-petrifies, and Stone_resistance is false, print the bare-handed wield message, name the cause, call instapetrify(), then return TRUE.
callers: wield.c:ready_weapon() calls cant_wield_corpse(wep) for a corpse before wielding it (line 183).
wield.c:can_twoweapon() contains a secondary-corpse call at line 794, but the preceding !TWOWEAPOK(uswapwep) guard makes that branch unreachable for corpses, as its source comment states.

evidence: Fresh replay at examined commit c849eb955ab487a30f2edd282ba9c3adf9cbf5a1: C/JS RNG calls match 2227/2227 and screens count 52/52; first screen and cursor mismatch is zero-based step 48, key “o”: C displays “--More--” after “You wield the cockatrice corpse in your bare hands.” while JS has no pager, with cursor C [59,0,1] and JS [39,19,1].

wield.c:cant_wield_corpse() (137-153) checks gloves, CORPSE type, touch_petrifies(), and Stone_resistance in C short-circuit order; it prints the bare-hand wield message, calls instapetrify(kbuf), then returns TRUE.

The production route is cmd.c wield dispatch -> wield.c:dowield() -> ready_weapon() -> cant_wield_corpse(). The JS helper exists at js/wield.js:cant_wield_corpse() and currently reaches note_unported('trap.c instapetrify') instead of awaiting the existing js/trap.js:instapetrify() call.
The only other direct C caller is the unreachable can_twoweapon() corpse branch; source line 794 explicitly says TWOWEAPOK() prevents it from being reached for corpses.
